rulings.challenge_claim: Both of this row's seams are crossed by byte-true devices that go undisclosed (heart-giving verb shared with 8:16; love/hatred bracket closing at 9:6; dead-token chain into 9:4-9:5), the internal 'one-event' echo is tier-overstated as byte when it is only accent_stripped/skeleton-identical, and the 'deed-in-hand formula' label is mismatched to a clause with no hand/deed lexeme.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes (verse_map_oshb.json + consonantal_index.json), all four sub-claims verify. (1) נָתַ֤תִּי (oshb:Eccl.8.16) and נָתַ֤תִּי (oshb:Eccl.9.1) are byte-identical codepoint-for-codepoint (differ only in the following particle, אֶת לִבִּי֙ vs אֶל לִבִּי֙) - an undisclosed cross-seam echo. (2) גַּֽם אַהֲבָ֣ה גַם שִׂנְאָ֗ה (oshb:Eccl.9.1) and גַּ֣ם אַהֲבָתָ֧ם גַּם שִׂנְאָתָ֛ם גַּם קִנְאָתָ֖ם (oshb:Eccl.9.6) are the ONLY three verses book-wide with love+hate co-occurrence (skeleton intersection re-swept independently: Eccl.3.8, Eccl.9.1, Eccl.9.6 - exact match to the challenge digit) - the row's own thesis phrase is one arm of a bracket closing 2 verses past its own rear seam, undisclosed. (3) הַמֵּתִֽים (9:3) / הַמֵּֽת (9:4) / וְהַמֵּתִ֞ים (9:5) form a real 'dead' token chain crossing the 9:3|9:4 seam (the OL claim that the bare-plural skeleton stands in exactly 3 verses conflates a prefixed variant - Eccl.9.5's form carries a vav the bare-skeleton match at Eccl.4.2/Eccl.9.3 does not - so 'exact skeleton, 3 verses' overstates precision; the underlying chain-across-the-seam claim is nonetheless correct). (4) TIER CHECK CONFIRMED: מִקְרֶ֨ה אֶחָ֜ד (9:2) and מִקְרֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד (9:3) differ in cantillation (independently verified codepoint-by-codepoint: word-final accent U+05A8 vs U+05A5, second-word accent U+059C vs U+0596) - the two are accent_stripped/skeleton-identical but NOT byte-identical, so the row's 'tier: byte' label and 'word-for-word' echo claim violate the TIER/ORDINAL DISCIPLINE standing rule. (5) LABEL CHECK CONFIRMED: the clause labeled 'deed-in-hand formula' is אֶל לִבִּי֙ - 'to my heart' - carrying no hand (yad) or deed/ma'aseh lexeme; that vocabulary belongs to the row's own later imperative bracket at 9:10, not here. LF's support verdict for this row did not engage any of these five points.
rulings.remedy: Add a device_notes disclosure of the two cross-seam echoes (heart-giving verb with 8:16; love/hate bracket forward to 9:6, noting the parallel dead-token chain forward into 9:4-9:5) per the standing CROSS-SEAM COHESION rule - disclosure only, no boundary change without boss adoption. Re-tier the 'one-event' recurrence citation from byte to accent_stripped/skeleton and add the book-level fate-refrain disclosure (same skeleton phrase also stands at 2:14 and 3:19, so it cannot alone carry row-bounding weight). Rename the 'deed-in-hand formula' label to an accurate term (e.g. 'heart-giving formula'). Test the cure must pass: citation_sweep.py/check_marks.py remain GREEN, and the corrected tier label matches collate.py's own tier output for the spliced phrase.

rulings.challenge_claim: The front-seam warrant rests on the English causal 'for' rather than a distinctive Hebrew form, and three byte-true devices (dead-token chain, love/hate bracket, portion/under-the-sun recurrence) cross this row's own seams undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes: (1) כִּֽי (mid-verse, 9:3), כִּי (opening, 9:4), and כִּ֧י (opening, 9:5) confirm ki is not distinctive at this exact seam - it recurs on both sides - so the row's sole cited warrant (the WEB 'For') is translation-dependent, not byte-engaged, matching the challenge. (2) The dead-token chain הַמֵּתִֽים/הַמֵּֽת/וְהַמֵּתִ֞ים (9:3-9:5) crosses this row's own front seam (same finding as P03-001's rear-seam side of the identical device). (3) גַּֽם אַהֲבָ֣ה גַם שִׂנְאָ֗ה (9:1) and גַּ֣ם אַהֲבָתָ֧ם גַּם שִׂנְאָתָ֛ם גַּם קִנְאָתָ֖ם (9:6) bracket the row's whole span (re-swept independently: exact 3-verse book-wide intersection Eccl.3.8/9.1/9.6). (4) וְחֵ֨לֶק (9:6) and חֶלְקְךָ֙ (9:9) share the chelek root; an independent skeleton re-sweep of chelek-family words returns exactly 8 verses book-wide (Eccl.2.10, 2.21, 3.22, 5.17, 5.18, 9.6, 9.9, 11.2), matching the challenge's digit precisely, and confirms a real undisclosed rear-seam echo (reinforced by the tachat-hashemesh refrain recurring at 9:6/9:9/9:11 per the staged inventory). LF's support verdict did not identify any of these.
rulings.remedy: Replace the WEB-only causal warrant with a Hebrew-engaged statement naming what IS distinctive about the 9:3|9:4 cut (the pivot from the shared 'one-event' thesis to the ketiv/qere-bearing hope-of-the-living clause), since ki itself is not diagnostic here. Disclose the dead-token chain at the front seam, the love/hate bracket spanning the row's whole span, and the chelek / tachat-hashemesh recurrence at the rear seam, per the CROSS-SEAM COHESION rule. Disclosure only; no boundary change without boss adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: The boundary holds, but the front-seam pairing is argued only from the English 'time' restatement rather than the byte-true et chain, and the '(sweep: 3 verses)' digit is attached to the bare pointed splice when it is really a blended-spelling family count.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes: עֵ֥ת (9:11), עִתּ֗וֹ (9:12, suffixed), and לְעֵ֣ת (9:12, prefixed) form a real byte-true chain the row's boundary_rationale never quotes (only the English 'time' restatement is given) - confirms the challenge. On the count-object point: eccl_device_inventory.json's own shavti_turns entry states count_object = "verses containing token shavti or veshavti" (count 3, refs Eccl.4.1/4.7/9.11) - i.e. the digit is for the BLENDED spelling family, not the single bare form שַׁ֜בְתִּי the row splices and footnotes '(sweep: 3 verses)' immediately after. This is exactly the SEMANTIC-CLASS COUNT DISCIPLINE violation the standing rules warn against (name the object - spelling vs family - before citing the count). LF's support verdict accepted the digit at face value without checking which object it was scoped to.
rulings.remedy: Quote the et/ito/le'et chain in the boundary_rationale rather than relying on the English restatement. Either quote the shavti_turns count_object's own family framing ('shavti or veshavti') alongside the digit, or scope the citation explicitly to the bare form (1 verse) if that is what is spliced. Disclose the rear-seam tachat-hashemesh (9:11/9:13) and chochma-root (9:11/9:13) recurrence in device_notes. Disclosure/precision fix only; the boundary itself is not contested.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the strongest_rejected_alternative for extending through 9:17 is a strawman naming only thematic proximity and omitting the true rival, a verbatim root-shama catchword bridging the seam. OL: the same catchword point, plus a second repeated lexeme (davar) and a byte-identical two-word frame (tova chochma) straddling the seam two verses further out.
rulings.grounds: LF and OL identify the SAME core defect (the row's stated rival understates the true strongest continuity signal at its own back seam); OL's version is a strict superset of LF's, adding two further byte-true signals. Independently re-derived: a skeleton sweep for the exact form נִשְׁמָעִֽים/נִשְׁמָעִ֑ים returns EXACTLY 2 verses book-wide (Eccl.9.16, Eccl.9.17) - confirming both primaries' claim that this catchword is book-unique to the seam. וּדְבָרָ֖יו (9:16) and דִּבְרֵ֣י (9:17) share the davar root (OL's second point) - confirmed present in the bytes, independent of the exact book-wide digit. Further independently verified: טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה (7:11), טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה (9:16), and טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה (9:18) are CODEPOINT-IDENTICAL at full byte tier (re-collated directly, not merely at skeleton) - the row's own closing judgment sits inside a byte-identical two-word frame whose second arm falls two verses past the row's own seam, at 9:18. This is genuine additional counter-evidence beyond what either primary quantified precisely, though it does not by itself compel a different boundary. The row's medium_low confidence and its own honest disclosure that 'a case for extending this unit through v.17 remains live' already registers some of this tension, but the stated rejected_alternative names the wrong evidence for it.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative to name the true strongest rival: the book-unique nishma'im skeleton pair (2 verses book-wide) plus the shared davar root, replacing the vague wisdom-despised/wisdom-praised theme framing. Additionally disclose (as texture, not as a unilateral boundary driver) that the byte-identical tova-chochma frame spans 9:16 and 9:18 (matching 7:11), which is live counter-evidence for a wider span - to be weighed at the boss/ owner level, not adopted here. Test the cure must pass: re-run collate.py on the corrected quotes to confirm byte tier, and confirm the rewritten rejected_alternative still honestly names v.16/v.17 as the genuinely contested seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the front-boundary rationale is accurate but omits the verbatim root-shama catchword bridging 9:16 into 9:17. OL: the row's rejected_alternative (aimed at v.18) rests on two false premises - that 9:17 shares a 'tov-comparative form' with 9:18 (it carries no tov-token at all), and that 9:17/9:18 share no repeated lexeme (the chochma root is shared).
rulings.grounds: LF and OL converge on ONE defect (the undisclosed nishma'im/davar catchword bridging back to 9:16, same evidence as P03-005's rear-seam side of the same device) and OL raises a SECOND, distinct defect LF did not identify. Independently re-verified via eccl_device_inventory.json's own tov_comparatives entries: tov_openers (12 refs) and tov_min_adjacent (6 refs) both EXCLUDE Eccl.9.17, and a direct skeleton scan of 9:17 confirms zero tov-family tokens anywhere in the verse - the row's rejected_alternative phrase 'shared tov-comparative form' misdescribes a construction 9:17 does not have (the WEB 'better than' rendering supplies a comparative the Hebrew mem-prefix alone carries). On repeated lexeme: חֲכָמִ֔ים (9:17) and חָכְמָ֖ה (9:18) do share the chochma root, confirmed present in both verses' skeleton, so 'share no repeated lexeme' is also false looking forward, not only backward to 9:16. Both OL sub-findings verify.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative in two parts: (1) name the real strongest rival - the nishma'im/davar catchword bridging BACK to 9:16 (same evidence disclosed at P03-005's remedy); (2) if the v.18 comparison is kept as a secondary point, correct its premises - 9:17 carries no tov-family token at all (per the tov_openers/tov_min_adjacent inventories), so drop 'shared tov-comparative form', and correct 'no repeated lexeme' since the chochma root recurs at 9:18. Disclosure/text correction only; the single_saying verdict itself is not contested.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the rejected alternative's 'share no repeated lexeme' claim between 9:18 and 10:1 is factually incorrect - both carry the chochma root. OL: the same point, PLUS the row's own device_notes/substrate signal is inverted - it claims tov_openers excludes 9:18, when 9:18's own first token is tov-family and the staged inventory explicitly includes it.
rulings.grounds: LF and OL converge on the repeated-lexeme defect (OL's version additionally names the shared little-versus-much mem-comparative shape); OL raises a SECOND, distinct, and more consequential defect LF did not catch. Independently re-verified: חָכְמָ֖ה (9:18) and מֵחָכְמָ֥ה (10:1) share the chochma root - confirmed present in both verses' bytes, so 'no repeated lexeme' is false (the digit-bearing citation of a 22-verse book-wide chochma-family sweep is the toolkit's own pre-verified figure, correctly reused by both primaries). SUBSTRATE-SIGNAL CHECK: eccl_device_inventory.json's tov_comparatives.tov_openers.refs list is ['Eccl.4.6','Eccl.4.13','Eccl.5.4','Eccl.6.9','Eccl.7.1','Eccl.7.2','Eccl.7.3','Eccl.7.5','Eccl.7.8','Eccl.7.11','Eccl.7.18','Eccl.9.18'] - Eccl.9.18 IS in the 12-verse list, and Eccl.9.18's own first skeleton token is tova - so the row's device_notes claim that 'tov_openers do not include 9:18 as opener' is a direct, machine-checkable contradiction of the staged inventory it purports to cite, not a matter of interpretation. This is more severe than a warrant-quality gap: observed_substrate_signals/device_notes are dependent fields expected to match the inventory exactly.
rulings.remedy: Correct device_notes/observed_substrate_signals to state that Eccl.9.18 IS a tov-opener per the staged inventory (12-verse list, tov_min_adjacent's mem-adjacency construction check is the correct reason it escapes THAT narrower 6-verse set - the two inventories answer different questions and must not be conflated). Correct strongest_rejected_alternative: 9:18 and 10:1 do share the chochma root; if single_saying is retained, restate the rejection on the correct ground (the shared lexeme is book-pervasive wisdom vocabulary carrying little diagnostic weight alone, per the 22-verse toolkit sweep) rather than claiming no shared lexeme exists. Test the cure must pass: re-run check_universals.py/citation_sweep.py (remain GREEN) plus a manual crosswalk of device_notes against eccl_device_inventory.json's tov_openers.refs.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF and OL both find the rejected_alternative's claim that 9:18 and 10:1 'share no repeated lexeme' is byte-false - both verses carry the chochma root.
rulings.grounds: LF and OL identify the SAME defect independently, with matching evidence and near-identical framing; no distinct sub-finding to separate. Independently re-verified: חָכְמָ֖ה (9:18, oshb:Eccl.9.18) and מֵחָכְמָ֥ה (10:1, oshb:Eccl.10.1) share the chochma root at word level (chochma / me-chochma with comparative mem), confirmed by direct skeleton comparison of the two verses. The 22-verse book-wide chochma-family sweep both primaries cite is the toolkit's own pre-verified digit for this object, correctly reused. The single_saying verdict itself is sound under the sentence-zone default; the defect is confined to the stated ground.
rulings.remedy: Correct rejected_alternative's 'for want of any repeated lexeme' claim - 9:18 and 10:1 share the chochma root. If single_saying is retained (recommended, per the sentence-zone default and the book-pervasiveness of the shared root), restate the rejection on the correct ground: the shared root is book-pervasive wisdom vocabulary (22-verse sweep) carrying little diagnostic weight alone, not an absence of shared lexeme.
